facts.statement: The genus Dactylobatus was described by B. A. Bean and A. C. Weed in 1909.
facts.quote: authority: B. A. Bean & A. C. Weed, 1909

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Dactylobatus is Dactylobatus armatus.
Dactylobatus is a genus of skates belonging to the family Rajidae.
facts.quote: Dactylobatus is a genus of skates in the family Rajidae.

facts.statement: These skates live in deep waters of the western Atlantic Ocean, ranging from Brazil to the United States and the Gulf of Mexico.
facts.quote: They are found in deep waters in the western Atlantic Ocean from Brazil to the United States, including the Gulf of Mexico.

facts.statement: Two species are currently recognized in the genus: Dactylobatus armatus, known as the skillet skate, and Dactylobatus clarkii, known as the hook skate.
facts.quote: Two species are recognized in this genus: Dactylobatus armatus B. A. Bean & A. C. Weed, 1909 (skillet skate) Dactylobatus clarkii (Bigelow & Schroeder, 1958) (hook skate)

facts.statement: Dactylobatus is a genus of fish in the family Rajidae and the order Rajiformes.
facts.quote: Dactylobatus es un género de peces de la familia de los Rajidae en el orden de los Rajiformes.

facts.statement: The species Dactylobatus armatus was described by Bean and Weed in 1909, while Dactylobatus clarkii was described by Bigelow and Schroeder in 1958.
facts.quote: Dactylobatus armatus (Bean & Weed, 1909) Dactylobatus clarkii (Bigelow & Schroeder, 1958)

facts.statement: The genus Dactylobatus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
No fossil occurrences for the genus Dactylobatus have been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
